<meta>continues from previous page: so that</meta> from there its powers, namely for expelling, may be rendered stronger, and furthermore the doses of <term>Mercurius præcipitatus</term> <gloss>precipitated mercury</gloss> may be more easily formed for administration or ingestion, specifically in the form of pills. This precipitated mercury is uniquely praised and commended here, and truly it performs very well. The same is achieved by <term>Mercurius vitæ</term> <gloss>Mercury of Life; a white powder derived from antimony</gloss> or the <term>flowers of butter of antimony</term> <gloss>sublimated antimony trichloride</gloss>, concerning which we spoke above, if 4 to 12 grains of it are administered for three full days in an extract of <term>Hellebore</term> <gloss>a plant used as a potent purgative</gloss> and <term>colocynth</term> <gloss>Bitter Apple; a powerful laxative fruit</gloss>; it successfully expels the resolved salt. Afterward, however, sweating and urination should be provoked with a decoction of <term>sarsaparilla</term>, <term>holy wood</term> <gloss>Guaiacum</gloss>, or <term>asarum</term> <gloss>wild ginger</gloss> root, always adding <term>spirit of Tartar</term> <gloss>a distillate of potassium bitartrate</gloss>, or other <term>diaphoretics</term> <gloss>sweat-inducing agents</gloss> and <term>diuretics</term> <gloss>urine-inducing agents</gloss>, as mentioned above. Especially effective is the addition of the <term>arcanum</term> <gloss>secret remedy</gloss> of <term>wormwood</term> or <term>blessed thistle</term>. Here it must be noted, however, that the three-day administration of <term>Mercurius vitæ</term> often tends to cause <term>prolapsus ani</term> <gloss>prolapse of the rectum</gloss> in adults, which is afterwards rarely or even with great difficulty cured. In treating <term>dropsy</term> <gloss>edema or fluid retention</gloss>, it is necessary that such purgatives be used immediately from the beginning of the cure: later, diuretics and <term>hydrotics</term> <gloss>water-expelling medicines</gloss> should follow. Otherwise, the <term>hysteron proteron</term> <gloss>the reverse of the natural order; putting the cart before the horse</gloss> would be practiced here; all the serum or water having flowed down to the kidneys and ureters, most persistent symptoms often arise there because of the heavy burden. Furthermore, in the preparation of the extract of the root of <term>Black Hellebore</term>, it is safer to take the wine itself instead of <term>spirit of wine</term> <gloss>ethanol</gloss>, in which the root itself should at least gently simmer without much noise; and this must be done with fresh wine until all the essential power has been extracted from the roots; afterward, the extract is to be reduced to the thickness of honey by evaporating or distilling. This is because <term>spirit of wine</term>, on account of the fact that it prevails in <term>sulfur</term> <gloss>the flammable, oily principle in alchemy</gloss> rather than in <term>liquor</term> <gloss>solvent fluid</gloss>...

<summary>Crollius describes the use of precipitated mercury and antimony-based compounds for purging fluid in dropsy patients, warning against improper sequencing of treatments that could damage the kidneys. He provides specific instructions on extracting Black Hellebore using wine to create a medicinal syrup.</summary>
<keywords>Precipitated Mercury, Mercury of Life, Antimony, Black Hellebore, Colocynth, Dropsy, Hydrops, Diuretics, Purgatives, Pharmaceutical extraction</keywords>
